steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Shahadah is the first and most important Pillar of Islam: "There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is his messenger." This declaration is said daily in prayer and is the only thing required to become a Muslim.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — The Five Pillars
steps.body: 1. For The Five Pillars questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of The Five Pillars to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: When Malcolm X converted to Islam in 1964, he recited the Shahadah to formally become a Muslim. This simple declaration transformed his identity and worldview. In the UK today, new Muslims recite the Shahadah at mosques across the country, with the London Central Mosque reporting approximately 200 conversions per year.

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: In the UK, both Sunni and Shi’a mosques are found in major cities. The London Central Mosque in Regent’s Park is predominantly Sunni, while the Islamic Centre of England in London serves the Shi’a community. Both communities observe Ramadan and perform Hajj, but their additional practices differ.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain why the Shahadah is the most important Pillar of Islam.

steps.title: Check your answers

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
